headline: The restart run remains a single touch, not yet a rhythm. Strength is now over two weeks cold. The Åre base still carries you, but the open gaps haven't moved.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is one of a heavy summer block still cooling in the background rather than a week actively building. The recent four-week running total dwarfs the prior stretch, but almost all of that weight comes from the Åre back-to-back giant days — the current week holds only a short, controlled Copenhagen restart. That run did its job: it sat easy and reintroduced turnover without straining anything. Strength, though, is the piece that keeps slipping — no session in over two weeks, and the streak stays at zero against a year-to-date cadence that used to be more regular. Steps stay high and consistent even on rest days, so genuine daily movement isn't the problem; it's structured stimulus that's thin. Nothing here signals lost fitness — the base is real — but the load is currently narrow, resting almost entirely on one modality's echo.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is spiky rather than smoothly progressive: a massive endurance spike in mid-August followed by a near-stall. That's consistent with a big deliberate block absorbed and now digesting, not with irregular or lost training. Year-to-date, the distance gap over last year is enormous, which tells you the base has genuinely expanded across the season. The question the shape raises is whether the coming weeks re-distribute effort back into a repeatable weekly rhythm, or whether the pattern of big blocks separated by gaps continues. For year-round hybrid readiness, the former serves you better than another burst.
sections.threshold: The threshold read is now two months old and unchanged simply because nothing has challenged it. The recent runs that touched Z3 and Z4 — the two late-August efforts — were short and hilly rather than sustained tempo, so they don't refresh the number. Your demonstrated aerobic ceiling from earlier this year remains intact; there's no evidence of decline, but equally no fresh data to confirm it's climbed. Until a sustained effort at controlled hard pace appears, this figure is a placeholder, not a current reading.
sections.zones: The weekly distribution is dominated by the huge low-intensity Åre volume, which is exactly right for what that block was — time on feet, deep Z1. The two late-August runs were the only genuinely mixed-intensity sessions, and their shape — real Z3/Z4 minutes with Z1/Z2 around them — reads as rolling terrain rather than a structured tempo. The restart run sat cleanly in easy territory, appropriate for a re-entry. What's missing from the recent mix isn't easy volume, it's a deliberate sustained threshold block. The grey-zone exposure is minimal, which is fine.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR history shows the familiar controlled pattern — sessions living mostly in Z1 with occasional Z2/Z3 spikes, typical of functional work. Nothing anomalous there, and no strength session recent enough to add a new data point. On the run side there's no source disagreement worth flagging this week. Nothing notable in the HR patterns beyond the absence of recent strength data itself.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the clearer story than any single metric: a dense clustering of activity in mid-August, then a sparse stretch broken only by one run. This is the burst-and-gap pattern flagged before, and it hasn't yet resolved. The running streak survives on frequency-of-weeks, but within-week distribution is thin right now. Whether the next stretch spreads load across days rather than stacking it is the thing actually worth watching in the shape.
sections.personal_bests: Your speed PBs date from last autumn, and nothing in the current mix — heavy easy volume plus one restart — points toward them being in reach this moment. That's not a concern; it reflects where the focus has been. The ultra-distance PB sits comfortably supported by the summer base. Speed PBs will only re-enter the conversation once sustained faster work returns to the week.

watch_items: Watch whether strength finally reappears — it's the longest-standing untouched gap and the streak still reads zero.
Watch whether a second and third run land close to the restart, turning one touch into an actual weekly rhythm.
Watch whether the burst-and-gap calendar pattern gives way to load spread across the week.
Watch whether any sustained tempo shows up to refresh the now two-month-old threshold read.
